name: Virtual PET Patients
eli5: Turn a real scan into a LEGO-model patient that a computer scanner can scan again, with a person checking every step.
summary: Human-in-the-loop agentic framework that converts retrospective PET/CT into auditable patient models (anatomy, functional regions, activity, attenuation), runs CASSOULET simulations, and writes quantitative validation reports. Groundwork for NASGM-style learned simulators and PAD-style heterogeneous PET synthesis.
facts: 8 agent roles with human QC gates

more.problem: Building realistic virtual patients for PET simulation by hand takes days per subject and leaves little record of the choices made.
approach: A coordinator agent dispatches inventory, segmentation, QC, activity-map, simulation and validation agents
Four separate layers per patient: anatomy, functional regions, activity, attenuation; original labels are never overwritten
Human QC gates after anatomy, after activity, and before any result is released
Every step leaves hashes, before/after images and a reason
status: 11-subject GE DMI/OMNI cohort in preparation; 162 functional compartments drafted
Next: one end-to-end simulation and quantitative report, then reproducibility tests
Later: a learned surrogate of the simulator (NASGM-style) and heterogeneous PET synthesis (PAD-style)

name: CASSOULET
eli5: A flight simulator, but for PET scanners.
summary: Compositional Anthropomorphic Spatial Synthesizer for ground-truth Lesion Export. GPU PET/CT simulator with scanner models of GE DMI 5R, GE OMNI and Siemens Quadra: DOI, TOF single-scatter, BSREM/OSEM, CT simulation, DICOM export.

more.problem: Commercial PET simulators are closed, slow to adapt, and can't insert heterogeneous or patient-shaped lesions on modern scanners.
approach: Analytical PET/CT simulation with scanner models of GE Discovery MI 5-ring, GE OMNI Legend and Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra
Physics v2: depth-of-interaction sub-LORs, TOF single-scatter, crystal normalisation, randoms
BSREM and OSEM reconstruction, CT simulation and attenuation, DICOM export
GPU runs on Colab A100/T4 orchestrated by agents, with a written constitution for every study
status: More than 150 dated studies in October 2026
Multicentre virtual testbench manuscripts in preparation

name: VeriTomiX
eli5: A driving test for medical-imaging AI before it meets real patients.
summary: Benchmarking-as-a-service for imaging devices and AI, built on CASSOULET and 3D-printed phantom evidence.

more.problem: Imaging AI and scanners are rarely tested against a ground truth before they reach patients.
approach: Benchmarking as a service built on CASSOULET simulation and 3D-printed phantom evidence
Shared phantom designs and virtual testbenches give every site and vendor the same reference
status: Concept and evidence stage: strategy, grant and evidence decks prepared

name: VeriTomiX Virtual Office
eli5: A tiny company where all the coworkers are AI, and I'm the boss who signs off.
summary: Native macOS app running a company of 8 AI department heads (R&D, Phantoms, Product, Clinical, Partnerships, IP/Ops, Management, Finance) on Codex and Gemini CLIs, with local Llama specialists, meetings, task queues and GPU allocation.

more.problem: Running a venture's research, product, IP and finance work alone means constant context switching.
approach: A native macOS app that runs a small company of AI department heads: R&D, Phantoms, Product, Clinical, Partnerships, IP/Ops, Management and Finance
Department heads run on Codex and Gemini CLIs; each department has a local Llama 3.2 specialist through Ollama for private, cheap tasks
Meetings, task queues, GPU allocation, Whisper transcription and deliverables folders
The founder approves; agents propose
status: In daily use for VeriTomiX planning and evidence work

figures.caption: The office floor: each department has a room; agents move between desk, coffee and break rooms, and the founder chats with any of them. Here Mira summarises a study from a vault document with its SHA-256 provenance.
Meetings: agents present completed studies as slide decks with results and limitations, and can present them live with narration.

hierarchy.does: Sets priorities, approves results, can pause the office or hit the emergency stop
Breaks requests into tasks, assigns departments, runs meetings and the weekly review

hierarchy.who: Mira (R&D), Noah (Phantoms), Ada (Product), Lina (Clinical), Leo (Partnerships), Iris (IP & operations), Finn (Finance)
hierarchy.does: Own their department's work and deliverables
hierarchy.model: Codex CLI for R&D; Gemini CLI for the others

hierarchy.does: Evidence extraction and small support tasks, kept private and free

deployment: A native macOS app that keeps a background office running, with a start/stop launcher
Each agent runs as its own CLI session; a shared execution queue, per-agent locks and GPU allocation stop them colliding
Local Python workers handle numerical jobs (regression, maths) so results are computed, not guessed
Whisper transcribes meetings; slides are exported for live presentation
Documents enter a vault with SHA-256 hashes so every answer can be traced to its source
safeguards: Capabilities and grants per agent; the founder approves anything consequential
Audit ledger of actions and a monthly budget cap
Emergency stop and pause office controls
Explicit 'not clinical validation' labelling on generated material

name: ANIMUS Jobs
eli5: A job-hunting sidekick that finds jobs, checks they're real, and helps write the letter.
summary: Local-first AI career agent: multi-source discovery, AI web radar, link verification by Claude/Codex, tailored CVs and letters, Fellowship Match, kanban, calendar, and a game layer with XP and rarity tiers.

more.problem: Job and fellowship searching is scattered across dozens of sites, full of dead links, and hard to tailor applications for.
approach: Discovery from job APIs, company boards, France Travail, EU funding calls, OpenAlex and job-alert emails
An AI web radar searches the web lane by lane; Claude or Codex open postings to verify they're real
Tailored CVs, letters, outreach emails, mock interviews and a Fellowship Match for postdocs
Runs locally on your own AI subscriptions: no API bills, CV stays on your machine

figures.caption: ANIMUS world map: every verified opportunity pinned by location and type, scored against the CV, with remote and online listings alongside.

hierarchy.does: Swipe to triage, approve applications; your swipes train the ranking
Picks a model per task type, falls through on usage limits, login errors or daily budget
hierarchy.model: Claude CLI → Codex → Gemini → Anthropic API

hierarchy.does: For hard questions, each family answers and one synthesis is written
Fetch opportunities, score against the CV, verify links, draft CVs and letters

deployment: Runs locally: a FastAPI server and web UI, with data in a local SQLite database outside the repo
Uses the AI subscriptions you already have through their CLIs, so there are no API bills and the CV stays on your machine
Sources: job APIs, company boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby), France Travail, EU funding calls, OpenAlex for potential PIs, read-only job-alert emails, and an AI web radar
Daily per-agent budgets, cooldowns and health tracking for each model
safeguards: Gemini may only propose opportunities; Claude or Codex must approve them before they appear
A verifier archives dead, generic, duplicate or expired links and shows who added and who verified each item
Never invents facts about the candidate: everything comes from the stored resume
No scraping of sites whose terms forbid it

name: Flow Lab
eli5: Watch coloured dye flow through pipes like blood, then see how a scanner would picture it.
summary: Parametric pulsatile flow-phantom simulator with GUI: pulsatile flow, bladder-like storage, exchanging sphere, PET/CT quality animations.

more.problem: Dynamic and flow PET need ground truth for moving tracer, which static phantoms can't provide.
approach: A parametric flow-phantom simulator with a browser GUI
Pulsatile flow, bladder-like storage and an exchanging sphere
Generates tracer-transport animations, time-activity curves and PET/CT quality views automatically

name: Human FDG Digital Twin
eli5: A see-through computer body where sugar tracer travels through the blood and out through the kidneys.
summary: Coupled FDG circulation and renal excretion, vascular splines, organ TACs, and a WebGL anatomical atlas.

more.problem: Whole-body PET simulation needs a body whose tracer moves the way it does in people.
approach: One subject's anatomy from open data, segmented with TotalSegmentator and MOOSE
Arterial-input-driven renal subsystem first, then circulation detail, calibrated to published human time-activity curves
An interactive WebGL anatomy atlas for review
status: Prototype; staged approximation, not a full physiological model

name: MuPET
eli5: Use the physics of how stuff spreads to make realistic fake scans.
summary: Mass-transport physics for synthetic PET data generation.

name: Hepta Medical toolbox
summary: Predictive ablation models and a CT/MRI segmentation-visualisation toolbox.

name: AUV MEC
summary: Deputy team lead, autonomous underwater vehicle club.

name: Kage Game Dev Pipeline
eli5: Three AI coding agents build my game in parallel, check each other's work, and I approve every merge.
summary: A multi-agent game studio: Claude Code, Codex CLI and Antigravity take tasks from a ./crew board, each works in its own git worktree, and a different agent reviews the change before I merge it to main. Meshy AI and headless Blender scripts produce the 3D assets.
facts: No agent approves its own work

hierarchy.does: Game direction, lore, mechanics design, final merge gate approval, and asset review
Engine architecture, shader systems, camera damping, and scene composition
Combat state machines, locomotion, hitboxes, character controller, and test suites
Automated regression testing, git worktree peer review, and headless validation
T2 Smart Topology 3D generation (<=15k tris), auto-rigging, and headless glTF optimization

deployment: Local canonical repo with isolated git worktrees per agent task
Autonomous ./crew orchestrator managing tasks from todo -> running -> review -> approve
Headless Blender 5.2 Python scripts for automated glTF optimization and texture atlasing
Cross-agent peer review requiring another agent's approval before human merges to main
safeguards: Strict budget guards: <=150k triangles on screen, <=2 shadow-casting lights, 60 FPS target
Dry-run mandatory on paid Meshy AI credits before actual 3D generation runs
Read-only sandboxed review passes ensuring no agent self-approves code
Human review required for all final asset and code merges

more.problem: Solo indie 3D game development requires balancing 3D modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, physics, camera scripting, sound design, and shader engineering with limited time.
approach: Deploy a multi-agent crew where specialized CLI agents tackle discrete domains based on their reasoning strengths.
Integrate automated DCC pipelines (Blender headless + Meshy AI) to generate rigged characters without manual topology work.
Enforce strict Git worktree isolation with automated peer verification before human approval.
status: ./crew task orchestration running daily across Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity
Gameplay, the world and footage are on the Kage game page
